tools.name: Curiosity rover
tools.summary: Curiosity is a car-sized rover that has been exploring Gale Crater since 2012, studying whether Mars once had the right conditions for tiny living things.
facts: It landed in August 2012 using a rocket-powered 'sky crane' that lowered it on cables.
It is about the size of a small car and has a mass of roughly 900 kg.
A nuclear power source keeps it running day and night, even in dust storms.
It found evidence that Gale Crater once held a lake of liquid water.
Its ChemCam laser zaps rocks so scientists can learn what they are made of.

tools.name: Perseverance rover
tools.summary: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater in 2021 to look for signs of ancient life and to collect rock samples that a future mission could bring back to Earth.
facts: It landed on 18 February 2021 in Jezero Crater, which held a lake and river delta long ago.
It drills out rock cores and seals them in metal tubes for a possible return to Earth.
Its MOXIE experiment made oxygen from the carbon dioxide in the Martian air.
It carried the Ingenuity helicopter to Mars tucked under its belly.
Its microphones recorded the first sounds from the surface of Mars.

tools.name: Ingenuity helicopter
tools.summary: Ingenuity is a small robotic helicopter that proved powered flight is possible in the thin air of Mars. It was planned for 5 flights and ended up making 72.
facts: On 19 April 2021 it made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
It has a mass of only about 1.8 kg, lighter than most laptops with their chargers.
Its blades spin far faster than those of helicopters on Earth because the Martian air is so thin.
It completed 72 flights before rotor damage ended its mission in January 2024.
It carried a tiny piece of fabric from the Wright brothers' first aeroplane.

tools.name: InSight lander
tools.summary: InSight was a stationary lander that listened to the inside of Mars. Its seismometer recorded marsquakes, revealing the planet's crust, mantle and core.
facts: It landed on the flat plains of Elysium Planitia on 26 November 2018.
Its seismometer detected more than 1,300 marsquakes.
It stayed in one place: it had no wheels, only a robotic arm.
Its data showed that Mars has a liquid core.
The mission ended in December 2022 after dust covered its solar panels.

tools.name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module "Eagle"
tools.summary: Eagle is the spacecraft that carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to the Moon's surface on 20 July 1969, the first time people landed on another world.
facts: It touched down in the Sea of Tranquility on 20 July 1969.
Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21.5 hours on the surface.
Michael Collins stayed in orbit in the command module Columbia.
Its lower half, the descent stage, is still standing on the Moon today.

tools.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle
tools.summary: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was a battery-powered 'Moon buggy' that astronauts drove on Apollo 15, 16 and 17, letting them explore much farther from their lander.
facts: It was first driven on the Moon in 1971 during Apollo 15.
It flew on three missions: Apollo 15, 16 and 17.
It folded up to fit on the side of the lunar module for the trip to the Moon.
It ran on electric batteries and its wheels were made of woven metal mesh, not rubber.
All three rovers were left behind and are still on the Moon.

tools.name: Apollo laser retroreflector
tools.summary: Apollo astronauts left panels of special mirrors on the Moon. Scientists still bounce laser beams off them to measure the distance to the Moon very precisely.
facts: Apollo 11, 14 and 15 each left a retroreflector array on the surface.
The Apollo 14 array, placed at Fra Mauro in 1971, holds 100 small glass prisms.
It needs no power, which is why it still works more than 50 years later.
The measurements show the Moon is drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 cm each year.

tools.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander
tools.summary: Vikram is the Indian lander that touched down near the Moon's south pole in 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon.
facts: It landed on 23 August 2023, closer to the lunar south pole than any earlier lander.
It carried a small six-wheeled rover named Pragyan.
It was built to work for one lunar day, which is about 14 Earth days.
Its instruments measured the temperature of the lunar soil near the south pole.

tools.name: Apollo 14 Lunar Module "Antares"
tools.summary: Antares is the lunar module that landed Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell in the hilly Fra Mauro region in February 1971, on the third crewed Moon landing.
facts: It landed at Fra Mauro on 5 February 1971.
Shepard and Mitchell spent about 33 hours on the surface and made two moonwalks.
The crew pulled a two-wheeled cart to carry tools and rock samples.
Stuart Roosa stayed in orbit in the command module Kitty Hawk.

tools.name: Hasselblad lunar camera
tools.summary: Apollo astronauts photographed the Moon with specially modified Hasselblad cameras that used wide 70 mm film. Almost every famous picture from the lunar surface was taken with one.
facts: Apollo crews used modified Hasselblad 500EL cameras loaded with 70 mm film.
The cameras used on the surface had no viewfinder: astronauts wore them on the chest and aimed by turning their bodies.
To save weight for Moon rocks, crews left the camera bodies on the Moon and brought home only the film magazines.
Each film magazine was marked with a letter, and a label on top listed the settings for sunlight and shadow.
